name: Saver Automotive Products
old_description: Select your Year, Make & Model to find matching wiper blades for your vehicle:
about:
Saver Automotive Products is based in Halethorpe, Maryland, where it was incorporated in 1991 as a family‑owned business. The company began as a parts supplier to other wiper blade manufacturers before transitioning to its own manufacturing operation in 2007.

Today the company produces and assembles the majority of its windshield wiper blades in the United States, a distinction it claims as the only wiper blade manufacturer to do so. Its product lines cover beam, hybrid, conventional, air‑foil, and winter blades for passenger vehicles, plus heavy‑duty commercial blades for buses and trucks. Saver also serves as the exclusive licensee for Pennzoil‑ and Quaker State‑branded wiper blades.

The company sells through traditional automotive distributors, buying groups, retailers, and original‑equipment suppliers, providing coverage for both early and late‑model vehicles. Its customer base spans the automotive aftermarket, commercial fleet operators, and OEM channels.

Saver emphasizes its domestic production footprint and licensed‑brand portfolio as key differentiators, aiming to deliver high‑quality, reliable wiper products that meet evolving market needs.

name: Savory Concepts LLC dba Quality Foods
old_description: “A unique fresh food program with snacks, candy and beverages offered through a micro-market or vending concept.”
about:
Savory Concepts LLC, doing business as Quality Foods, has operated from Bristol, Connecticut since 1991. The company is led by President Peter Graziano and Administrative Vice President Michele Graziano, a principal of the firm, who oversee a commissary that designs menus, develops recipes, and manages food production for workplace refreshment programs across Connecticut, Massachusetts, and Rhode Island.

The business provides fresh food programs through two primary channels: micro‑markets — self‑serve convenience‑store‑style installations — and traditional vending machines, supplemented by office coffee service. A dedicated culinary center prepares breakfast, lunch, and dinner items, handling menu design, research and development, purchasing, quality control, packaging, and sanitation. Service technicians maintain vending and micro‑market equipment, while a fleet department keeps delivery trucks operational for daily routes.

Customers are employers in southern New England seeking turnkey workplace dining solutions. The company cites offices and facilities throughout CT, western MA, and RI as its core market, with sales efforts led by Vice President Rosina Cavallo, who brings over three decades of business development experience in the region.

The firm emphasizes a “unique and wholesome food program” tailored to an industry with special application, pursuing excellence through continuous learning and timely service response. Its stated goal is that each customer enjoys the product, the service, and the interaction with its people.

The family-owned business began as a woodcarving operation before evolving into a contract furniture manufacturer serving the commercial market.

Today the company produces a broad line of contract furniture, with a catalog that includes items such as the 5480-REST, UR-ML2020-20-QS, 2805-HPSE-QS, and BBS-SAFE-QS series. Its manufacturing capabilities encompass wood furniture fabrication, machine woodcarving, and assembly, all backed by a limited lifetime warranty on products it manufactures to the original purchaser.

about:
Sawtooth Wood Products operates from Bellevue, Idaho, in the Wood River Valley. The company traces its roots to Bob Parker, who established the business as a log construction specialist serving Ketchum, Hailey, Sun Valley, and Bellevue. The current owner, a former Boise State Broncos running back who played in the 2007 Fiesta Bowl, took over the company after growing up on his grandparents' Idaho ranch. He brought a philosophy of optimal performance shaped by athletics and agricultural work.

The firm provides two core services: custom log construction of homes and buildings, and fence installation ranging from residential picket fences to commercial security fencing. Each project is approached as a customized solution, with the team working directly with clients to match specific design and functional requirements. The company does not disclose facility size, headcount, or annual volume.

Customers include homeowners and businesses throughout the Wood River Valley. Examples cited by the company include backyard picket fences for residences and large security fences for commercial properties, as well as one-of-a-kind log homes that reflect the region's architectural character.

The owner cites his football background — teamwork, perseverance, attention to detail, and handling pressure — as directly applicable to construction craftsmanship. The company emphasizes carrying forward Bob Parker's legacy, using quality materials and focusing on optimal performance in every detail. The driving force is described as the passion and dedication the team puts into each piece of wood.

name: Schanz Furniture & Refinishing
old_description: Schanz Furniture & Refinishing — Handcrafted Hardwood Since 1965
about:
Schanz Furniture & Refinishing has operated in South Amana, Iowa, since 1965, when Norman and Joanna Schanz began crafting furniture in their basement. The family-owned workshop remains in the hands of the second generation, Mike and Michelle Schanz, and is situated in the historic Amana Colonies.

The shop produces custom solid-hardwood furniture — primarily cherry, oak, and walnut — along with furniture repair, refinishing, and traditional chair caning and seat weaving. Every piece is built start-to-finish by a single craftsman using traditional joinery and a proprietary formaldehyde-free conversion varnish applied in multiple hand-sanded coats. Repairs and refinishing are performed only in the shop; small gift items such as cutting boards and cheese slicers ship nationwide, while furniture is available for pickup or scheduled delivery.

Customers include homeowners commissioning one-of-a-kind dining suites or restoring heirloom pieces, tourists visiting the Amana Colonies, and gift buyers ordering small goods online. The business also serves clients seeking traditional seat-weaving patterns such as hole caning, pressed cane, rush, and splint.

The company emphasizes that its furniture is built to outlast trends and mass-produced alternatives, citing a commitment to transparency — visitors can watch the craft process — and a refusal to use particle board, MDF, or painted finishes.

name: Scherer Metals - 1299 E. 58th Avenue, Denver
old_description: Founded in 1896, Scherer Metals has a rich history shaped by generations of dedicated leadership; from its early days under Frank Scherer & Sons, to the stewardship of the Koenig family, and beyond. We are proud to carry that legacy forward with the same passion, craftsmanship, and commitment to excellence that have defined us for over a century.
about:
Scherer Metals operates from Denver, Colorado, where it was founded in 1896 as Frank Scherer & Sons. The business passed to the Koenig family, which has stewarded the company through multiple generations, maintaining a focus on architectural metal fabrication.

The shop provides custom architectural and decorative metal fabrication, including shearing, punching, bending, polishing, MIG and TIG welding, and patina finishing. On-staff draftsmen and engineers translate concepts into build-ready designs, while project managers oversee complex jobs from start to finish. The facility also handles restoration and repair of existing metal components and stocks finishing materials such as corner guards and kick plates.

Scherer Metals serves architects, contractors, and designers across commercial and residential projects. Its portfolio includes railings, cladding, furniture, and decorative metalwork, with patina finishes applied using Sculpt Nouveau products, which the company distributes.

The company cites its 129-year history and certified welding staff as key differentiators, emphasizing on-time delivery and the ability to turn client visions into reality. As a distributor of Sculpt Nouveau metal paints, patinas, and clear coats, it offers a single source for both fabrication and specialty finishes.

name: Schlotterbeck & Foss Co
old_description: Handcrafting the Highest Quality Specialty Foods and Flavorings Since 1866
about:
Schlotterbeck & Foss Co. has operated from Westbrook, Maine since 1866, when Augustus G. Schlotterbeck and Charles S. Foss opened a prescription apothecary shop. The partners built a reputation for quality handcrafted products and fair dealings, later expanding into patented medicines and flavoring extracts in the 20th century. The business remains privately held.

Today the company manufactures a range of specialty foods including chef sauces, marinades, condiments, cooking sauces, artisan salsas, spreads, dessert sauces, and dressings. Its core competency lies in product development and proprietary small‑batch manufacturing, using a preparation, cooking, and packaging process designed to retain the shape, texture, and flavor of large‑cut ingredients such as blueberries, corn, mango, and whole garlic cloves. Formulations emphasize organic, non‑GMO, and clean‑label ingredients with no preservatives or artificial colors.

The company serves natural and conventional grocery retailers, club stores, and food‑service operators through private‑label programs and its own branded lines. Customers include national retail chains seeking differentiated gourmet products, as well as restaurants and institutional buyers looking for premium sauces and condiments.

Schlotterbeck & Foss traces its differentiation to over 150 years of continuous experience, artisan handcrafting methods, and a focus on ingredient integrity that it says cannot be replicated by competitors.

name: Schmidt Equipment & Supply
old_description: The Schmidt Family has been in the meat and food processing industry since 1943 when Roy Elias Schmidt and his partner, Leo Welch, opened The Schmidt-Welch Equipment Company to rebuild and service equipment in the St. Louis area during WWII. A few years later, Roy bought out his partner, and the company name was changed to Roy E. Schmidt Sales & Service Co.
about:
Schmidt Equipment & Supply traces its roots to 1943 in St. Louis, Missouri, when Roy Elias Schmidt and Leo Welch founded the Schmidt‑Welch Equipment Company to rebuild and service meat‑processing machinery during World War II. Welch soon sold his share to Schmidt, and the firm became Roy E. Schmidt Sales & Service Co. The business has remained in the Schmidt family for three generations.

Today the company operates as a single‑source distributor and service provider for the meat and food processing sectors. Its product lineup includes hydraulic stuffers, smokehouses, grinders, slicers, band saws, vacuum sealers, tumblers, mixers, injectors, patty molders, batter and breading systems, and a full range of supplies such as casings, seasonings, packaging materials, and cutting tools. A parts department sources components from major brands, and a service team offers scheduled maintenance and emergency after‑hours calls. The operation runs from a facility that houses a test kitchen and demonstration lab, serving customers within a 150‑mile radius of St. Louis across Missouri and Illinois.

The customer base spans commercial meat processors, sausage makers, and food manufacturers producing items such as salami, summer sausage, capicola, mortadella, bologna, and pork rolls. The company does not disclose specific client names but emphasizes its coverage of the Missouri and Illinois markets.

The firm highlights its family‑owned continuity, over 80 years of industry experience, a full test kitchen for product trials, and a commitment to supplying the newest equipment at competitive prices. Emergency service availability on weekends and after hours is also promoted as a key differentiator.
